text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Friday 2.81 percent higher from last week with stocks pursuing their upward trend bolstered by an illiquid market, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 517.54 points, up from 503.36 points last Friday.
"We would welcome new flotations because our clients do not know what to buy with only few shares traded each day," a broker at Casablanca-based Sogebourse said.
ONA group, the biggest private holding, was up five dirhams at 640 dirhams. It took 15 dirhams on the week.
Upline Securities said in a recent report that ONA net earnings are expected to reach 852 million dirhams ($92.6 million) in 1996 from 602 million dirhams in 1995.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, shed two dirhams to 596 dirhams. It fell eight dirhams during the week.
The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.6 billion dirhams.

Brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc jumped 56 dirhams to 1,926 dirhams. The firm announced on Thursday it had purchased 80 percent of soft drinks firm Societe Industrielle Marocaine (SIM) for $52 million). It controls 95 percent of Morocco's beer market. It also manufactures under licence Coca Cola and Heineken brands.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie gained 11 dirhams to 393 dirhams, adding 28 dirhams from last Friday.
Leading stock Wafabank dipped 13 dirhams to 675 dirhams after two days of significant gains but it soared 45 dirhams on the week.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a blue chip stock, took 3 dirhams to trade at 475 dirhams, up 15 dirhams from the previous week.
Samir oil refinery, the country's main refinery, gained eight dirhams to close at 279 dirhams. It gained 27 dirhams since last Friday.
Newly-floated Credor advanced by 23 dirhams to 623 dirhams, up 12 dirhams on the week.
"Credor is readjusting after having soared to unexpected highs," a trader said.
Traded volume on the official market was 99.9 million dirhams, up from 48.7 million dirhams last Friday.
